podcast.title: 2002 Breakup and Contractual Obligations
podcast.body: In 2002, the romantic and professional relationship between Royce Immorce and Mar Brighton dissolved, leading to the band's initial separation. Despite this, they remained contractually bound to Eco Records for two more albums. This obligation compelled them to reunite under duress to record "Estaus" and also contributed to their ambiguous messaging about a potential return in early interviews, as neither was confident in their ability to launch successful solo careers and wanted to avoid contract breaches. "El problema viene en 2002 cuando la pareja se rompe por motivos personales pero también profesionales."

podcast.title: 2006 Strained Reunion
podcast.body: In 2006, Demoloco briefly reunited for a few months, not to create new material, but primarily because Eco Records demanded a final album to fulfill their contract. The label, being relatively small, considered Moloco a crucial financial asset from the 1990s. However, the members' intense animosity, exacerbated by Royce Immorce's newfound "euphoria" after her solo success with "El Rabidud," rendered new recordings impossible. This reunion instead resulted in the compilation album "Aléol Cataló" and a few separate promotional appearances. "Se juntaron en el 2006 y no les del 2005 para empezar a hacer algunas cosas por la agración de material fue completamente imposible."

podcast.title: Ambiguous Reunion Messages
podcast.body: Following the recording of "Estaus" and their initial breakup, Royce Immorce and Mar Brighton gave interviews where they stated they were separating but intentionally left the door open for a future return. This ambiguous stance was strategic, serving to avoid breaching their contract with Eco Records for a still-pending album and reflecting their uncertainty about their individual professional prospects outside of Moloco. "Y en esas entrevistas dieron un mensaje bastante ambigo, porque se separaban, pero dejaban mucho la puerta abierta a volver."

podcast.title: Formation and Early Success
podcast.body: Demoloco (also referred to as Moloco) was founded by Royce Immorce and Mar Brighton shortly after they met, concurrently becoming a romantic couple. The band enjoyed a successful run of seven years, achieving both strong commercial sales and positive critical reception, before internal issues led to their initial breakup. "La cosa pasó bastante bien y el poco de conocerse fundaron Moloco, aparte de gran pareja sentimental, y durante 7 años tuvieron bastante éxito tantas mentas como en crítica."

podcast.title: Post-Aléol Cataló Interviews
podcast.body: After the release of the "Aléol Cataló" compilation, interviews with Royce Immorce and Mar Brighton were largely conducted separately due to their extreme animosity, as they "couldn't even see each other." It was during these interviews that Royce Immorce definitively clarified her stance, stating she would not work with Mar Brighton again, effectively signaling the irreversible end of Moloco. "Tan más se llevaban que gran parte de las entrevistas que hicieron en el cataló con las hicieron los dos mil vósporos separados porque ya no se podía ni ver."
